prompt: Write one regex, used with String.matches, that decides whether a string is a plausible email address: local part, one @, dotted domain, and a letters-only TLD of length 2+. Complete isPlausibleEmail in EmailChecker.
explanation: String.matches anchors the pattern to the whole string, so nothing before or after the email can sneak through. The local part is one character class repeated with +, the @ is a literal, and the domain is a label followed by any number of dot-label groups plus a mandatory final dot and letters-only TLD -- which is what forces at least one dot. Inside a Java string literal a regex dot escape is written \. because the backslash itself must be escaped.
hints: matches() checks the whole string, so you do not need ^ or $. Sketch the shape first: local @ label (.label)* .tld
Character classes do the heavy lifting: [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ for the local part, [A-Za-z0-9-]+ for each domain label, [A-Za-z]{2,} for the TLD.
Require the last dot OUTSIDE the repeated group: ...(\.label)*\.[A-Za-z]{2,} -- that guarantees at least one dot and a letters-only ending.
